target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure (D122) covers customer concentrations, stating no single customer exceeded 10% in 2023, while citing historical concentrations for Kingston (12% in 2022) and WPG (11% in 2022/13%). The 2024 filings split this topic: D121 introduces the segment revenue table (contextual, but part of the concentration discussion structure); D122 states the current 2024 status (one customer at 10%) and reiterates the 2023 status (no customer >=10%); D123 provides the historical 2022 context (12% and 11% customers) which directly corresponds to the Kingston and WPG data in the 2023 record. These three 2024 disclosures collectively cover the same specific subject matter of customer revenue concentration thresholds and historical comparisons as the 2023 record.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, one customer accounted for approximately 24% and another for 16% of total consolidated accounts receivable, though the Company does not believe these balances represent significant credit risk due to past collection experience.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose significant customer concentration, but they measure it against different bases. MU reports that one customer accounted for 10% of total revenue in 2024, whereas AMD discloses that one customer accounted for approximately 24% of total consolidated accounts receivable as of the end of 2024. While both indicate reliance on major clients, MU's metric is revenue-based while AMD's is balance-sheet (receivables) based.

comparisons.peer_topic: Significant Customer Concentration in Revenue and Receivables
comparisons.peer_summary: One customer accounted for 18% and 21% of net accounts receivable as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023, respectively, and represented 28%, 21%, and 20% of net revenue in fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022. This customer's revenue was included in the semiconductor solutions segment.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO discloses a more extreme concentration risk than MU regarding both revenue and receivables. In fiscal 2024, one customer accounted for 28% of AVGO's net revenue and 18% of its net accounts receivable, compared to MU's single customer contributing 10% of total revenue. AVGO also explicitly notes this customer is within the semiconductor solutions segment, aligning with the semiconductor nature of the industry.

comparisons.peer_topic: Concentration of revenue with largest customers
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, substantially all revenue from the three largest customers originated from the sale of platforms and other components by Intel Products operating segments.
comparisons.comparison: INTC discusses concentration among its top three largest customers but focuses on the source of that revenue (platforms and components) rather than providing specific percentage thresholds like MU. MU explicitly quantifies the concentration with one customer at 10% of total revenue. In contrast, INTC states 'substantially all' revenue from its three largest customers came from Intel Products segments, indicating high concentration without disclosing the exact percentage of total revenue attributable to them.
